subject: Order Form redlines: remedy tiers, IP carve-out, and notice routing
messages:
From: Claire Bates <claire.bates@brightwave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Kim <brian.kim@brightwave.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BrightWave Order Form — redlines and a couple of asks

Hi Irene / Aditya,

Attached are our redlines to the Order Form and a short note from Legal. Two items we want to clarify before we move to signature:

1) Liability cap carve-out for IP claims — our counsel is pushing for the cap to be excluded for "liability arising from a third-party claim of IP infringement where Customer is seeking recovery of royalties or other ongoing damages." They want this to be uncapped for any IP indemnity relating to patented/ copyrighted material.

2) Notice and remedy routing — we want an explicit 30-day cure period and a provision that allows Customer to pursue equitable relief if Redwood does not timely indemnify.

We highlighted the proposed language in the attached Word. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (a) whether an IP indemnity should be unlimited for royalty recovery, and (b) whether you can accept the 30-day cure plus express injunctive carve-out?

Attachments: BrightWave_OrderForm_Redlines_v2.docx, remedy-tier-proposal.pdf

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Bates
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightWave Inc.
claire.bates@brightwave.com
(415) 555-0199

Note: BrightWave Legal also asks that any escrow or escrow-like remedy be addressed in the MSA rather than the Order Form.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bates <claire.bates@brightwave.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightWave Order Form — redlines and a couple of asks

Hi Claire — thanks for the redlines and the clarity. Quick responses below and copied Aditya for commercial alignment.

1) IP indemnity / royalty recovery: Redwood position (high level) — we will indemnify and defend for third-party IP claims for models/services we deliver, and we typically exclude IP indemnity from the standard monetary liability cap. However, unlimited liability (open-ended royalty exposure) is a material ask. We are willing to accept an exclusion for IP indemnity but need to limit exposure to proven direct damages and reasonable royalty awards tied to the specific claim (and carve out punitive/consequential requests).

Proposed compromise language (high-level):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the monetary cap set forth in the Agreement shall not apply to (i) Customer's claims for third-party intellectual property infringement for which Redwood has an indemnification obligation under this Agreement; provided that Redwood's liability for such claims shall not exceed (A) amounts actually awarded by a final court judgment or (B) a reasonable royalty amount agreed in settlement with the claimant, in each case excluding consequential and exemplary damages."

2) 30-day cure + injunctive relief: We typically provide a 30-day cure window for non-IP operational issues. For IP claims, customers often seek faster or no-cure injunctive relief (e.g., immediate CEASE/RESTRAIN orders). We can accept explicit injunctive relief if: (a) Customer follows the notice and cooperation obligations in the MSA, and (b) Redwood has right to step-in/defend and seek replacement code/service where feasible.

Next steps: Aditya / I will take commercial feedback internally and then loop in Legal (Marissa) for redline language to send back. Claire, can you confirm whether BrightWave will accept the concept of a capped royalty exposure (court-awarded or agreed settlement) rather than fully unlimited royalties? Also confirm whether escrow language should be handled in the MSA as suggested.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
(650) 555-0104

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightWave Order Form — redlines and a couple of asks

Forwarding BrightWave's redlines and asks — they require guidance on IP indemnity exposure and the 30-day cure / injunctive carve-out. Key points to resolve:

- Customer wants unlimited exposure for "royalties or other ongoing damages" under IP infringement. They framed this as necessary to ensure recoverability of ongoing losses.
- They also want express injunctive relief even if Redwood is meeting cure/defense obligations.
- BrightWave Legal prefers escrow language to be in MSA; procurement included it in the Order Form redlines.

My proposed approach (for Legal to weigh in):
1) Keep IP indemnity outside the monetary cap but limit recoverable amounts to (i) final court judgment; or (ii) reasonable royalties agreed in settlement, subject to Redwood's right to defend. Explicitly exclude punitive, exemplary, and consequential damages from recoverable amounts unless otherwise required by law.

2) Accept 30-day notice/cure for operational issues. For IP claims: accept injunctive relief carve-out for situations where injunctive relief is the only adequate remedy, but include a requirement that Customer provide immediate notice and allow Redwood to (a) defend, or (b) propose mitigation/replacement. If Redwood can reasonably mitigate without an injunction, require good-faith discussion first.

3) Escrow: Agree to move escrow mechanics into the MSA and reference it from the Order Form.

Can you (Marissa) draft redline language that follows the above approach? Also flag any regulatory or insurance implications (e.g., open royalty exposure affecting our reins/indemnity insurance). Aditya — confirm that BrightWave is okay with the concept of a capped royalty exposure (court award or negotiated settlement).

Thanks,
Irene

--- Forwarded message attached: BrightWave_OrderForm_Redlines_v2.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWave Order Form — redlines and a couple of asks

Irene / Aditya — below is a redline snippet I prepared for the Order Form and a short comment on insurance. Feel free to paste into their doc and send back with cover note.

-- begin proposed redline snippet --
Section X.Y (Limitations on Liability)
"Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the aggregate liability of each party for any and all Claims arising under or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the aggregate Fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the Claim, except that the foregoing cap shall not apply to: (a) liability for a party's indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims of intellectual property infringement; provided, however, that Redwood's liability for such third-party IP infringement claims shall be limited to (i) amounts finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or (ii) a reasonable royalty amount agreed in settlement with the claimant, in each case excluding consequential, incidental, punitive and exemplary damages; and (b) liability for bodily injury or death resulting from willful misconduct."
-- end proposed redline snippet --

Insurance note: Our Professional Liability / E&O carrier has historically been comfortable with IP indemnities being outside the standard cap so long as we preserve our defense rights and have a settlement approval process. Unlimited royalty exposure, however, will likely be uninsurable and materially increases our commercial risk. If BrightWave insists on unlimited royalties we should: (1) ask Commercial for additional pricing/escrow; (2) involve Insurance to see if a tile policy is available; or (3) require a cap based on a multiple of average annual fees (e.g., 2x annual fees) as fallback.

Let me know if you want me to insert this into the doc and propose the settlement/court award language as final. I can also add a short cooperation and defense control clause to ensure we retain ability to manage the defense.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
